schemaNote: 2026 NFL draft pick ownership reconstructed as of the February 2026 offseason snapshot (after the 2025 season / Super Bowl LX, before the March 2026 league year). Ownership = original team plus every trade completed on or before 2026-02-28. March 2026 league-year trades and draft-day trades are NOT applied; they are listed in postFebruaryTrades so they can be replayed if wanted. Convenient fact: no 2026 pick changed hands between the 2025 trade deadline (Nov 4, 2025) and Mar 11, 2026, so this snapshot is stable for all of Nov 2025 - Feb 2026.
teamAbbrConvention: nflverse / roster_2025.csv style. Los Angeles Rams = "LA", Las Vegas Raiders = "LV", Kansas City = "KC", Green Bay = "GB", New Orleans = "NO", New England = "NE", San Francisco = "SF", Tampa Bay = "TB", Washington = "WAS", Jacksonville = "JAX", LA Chargers = "LAC".
draftOrderNote: Round-1 slot order listed by the team that ORIGINALLY owned each slot, per final 2025 standings and playoff finish: picks 1-18 = the 18 non-playoff teams by inverse record (strength-of-schedule tiebreak among the four 3-14 teams put LV 1st, NYJ 2nd, ARI 3rd, TEN 4th); 19-24 = wild-card losers by record (CAR, GB, PIT, LAC, PHI, JAX); 25-28 = divisional losers (CHI, BUF, SF, HOU); 29-30 = conference-championship losers (LA Rams, DEN); 31 = Super Bowl LX loser (NE); 32 = Super Bowl LX champion (SEA).

validation.structural: Exactly 224 non-compensatory picks = 7 per team, one per round for all 32 teams; 32 compensatory picks (max 4 for any team: BAL, PHI, PIT) + 1 Resolution JC-2A pick (Detroit, overall #100).
validation.recordsSum: 271 W / 271 L / 2 T = 544 team-games = 32 x 17. Self-consistent.
validation.csvReconciliation: ownerAtDraftApril2026 matches all 257 season=2026 rows of _sources/draft_picks.csv - 0 mismatches.
validation.februaryOwnershipSpotChecks: Compared against 12 archived Feb-2026 tankathon.com team pages via the Wayback Machine (CLE 2026-01-09, MIA 2026-01-19, JAX 2026-01-19, PIT 2026-02-02, WAS 2026-02-03, SEA 2026-02-08, LA 2026-02-08, SF 2026-02-14, DEN/NYG 2026-02-18, LV 2026-02-16, NE 2026-01-22). 6 teams matched exactly (CLE, MIA, NYG, LV, LA, PIT). The 6 differences are listed in caveats and none of them changes a team pick COUNT except the compensatory projections.

caveats: SOURCE CONFLICT (net-zero on counts): San Francisco held two 2026 sixth-rounders in 2025 (its own, slot #209, and Minnesota's, slot #198) and traded one to Washington (Aug 24, 2025, Brian Robinson Jr.) and one to New England (Oct 29, 2025, Keion White). Wikipedia says WAS got SF's own (#209) and NE got MIN's (#198); the Feb-2026 Tankathon pages say the opposite. Wikipedia's version is used because it reconciles with the actual draft (NE traded #198 to MIN mid-draft and WAS drafted at #209). Either way WAS and NE each hold exactly one extra sixth-rounder in February.

SOURCE CONFLICT (net-zero on counts): Seattle holds exactly one sixth-round pick in February in both sources, but Wikipedia says it is Cleveland's #188 (acquired Aug 11, 2024, Nick Harris trade) with Seattle's own #213 having gone to Jacksonville (Oct 14, 2024, Roy Robertson-Harris) and on to Detroit (Apr 25, 2025), while Tankathon shows Seattle holding its own late-round-6 slot. Wikipedia is used - it reconciles with the final draft (#188 was ultimately drafted by NYJ via Seattle, #213 by CHI via Detroit).

SOURCE CONFLICT: the Jan 19, 2026 Tankathon page shows Jacksonville with 9 picks, missing JAX's own seventh (#240) and Philadelphia's sixth (#203, acquired Sept 9, 2025 in the Tank Bigsby trade). The final draft confirms JAX owned both (JAX drafted at #203 and #240 with no intervening trade), so both are kept. Treat JAX = 11 February picks as the better-supported number.

The 32 compensatory picks and the 1 Resolution JC-2A pick (overall #100) were not officially awarded until March 2026. They ARE included here (needed to run a full 257-pick draft) but each carries an "uncertain: ... not officially awarded until March 2026" note in viaTradeNote. Their February owner is the team later awarded them, except #100 which Detroit had already traded to Jacksonville on April 25, 2025.

Source annotation limit: Wikipedia annotates a pick only when its FINAL owner differs from the original owner. A pick traded away and then re-acquired by its original team before February 2026 would leave no trace and would show here as untraded. No such case is known, but it cannot be ruled out from these sources.

Overall pick numbers for rounds 3-7 reflect the final April 2026 slotting, which depends on the March 2026 compensatory award. In a strict February snapshot only the 224 non-compensatory slots were fixed.
Wikipedia labels the NY Jets -> Detroit trade of pick #44 as "(PD)" but dates it April 24, 2026 (mid-draft). Treated as post-February either way.
